answer: The bug was in `middleware/recoverer.go` within the `parse` method of `prettyStack`. The first call to `cW` (which writes a newline) had its second argument hardcoded to `true`, causing ANSI color codes to be included even when `useColor` was set to `false`. I updated this line to use the `useColor` variable.

The bug was in `middleware/recoverer.go` within the `parse` method. The first call to `cW` (which writes a newline) had its `useColor` parameter hardcoded to `true`, causing ANSI color codes to be emitted even when `NoColor` was set to true by the user. I changed this to `false`.

The bug was in `middleware/recoverer.go` within the `parse` method of the `prettyStack` struct. Specifically, several calls to `cW` (which writes colored or uncolored text) were hardcoded with `true` for the `useColor` parameter instead of using the `useColor` argument passed to the function. This caused ANSI color codes to be included in the output even when `NoColor` was set to true. I updated these calls to use the `useColor` variable.

The bug was in `middleware/recoverer.go` where the first line of the panic message was being printed with color even when `useColor` was false. I changed `cW(buf, true, bRed, "\n")` to `cW(buf, false, bRed, "\n")`.
